classification.difficultyReason: Read frequencies from a column graph and use cumulative counts to locate the two middle observations.

content.prompt: The marks obtained for a quiz by a group of students are displayed in the column graph.

spec.description: Discrete columns with horizontal grid lines at 0, 2, 4 and 6. Marks 4 through 10 are equally spaced; mark 9 has no positive column. Source turquoise fill and blue outlines are mapped to the standard blue series palette.
spec.answerVisibility: All columns and axis values are permanent givens; no answers are highlighted.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many students had their marks recorded?

answer.worked:
The total number of students is the sum of the frequencies.

$$2+6+6+4+4+0+2=24$$

24 students had their marks recorded.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the median of the marks?

answer.worked:
There are 24 marks, so the median is the average of the 12th and 13th values in numerical order. There are 2 values of 4 and 6 values of 5, giving 8 values below 6. The next 6 values are all 6, occupying positions 9–14. Both middle values are therefore 6.

$$\text{Median}=\frac{6+6}{2}=6\text{ marks}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the mode of the marks?

answer.worked: The highest frequency is 6 students. Marks of 5 and 6 both have this frequency, so the modes are 5 and 6 marks.
